summary_rationale: Qualcomm combines an elite 31.1% ROIC and a 72.4%-EBT-margin QTL licensing vault (renewals with Apple, Huawei, and Transsion locked through FY2030–2033) with a cyclical fabless QCT semiconductor engine ($37.21B FY26 revenue). While Automotive surged 51.7% YoY to $6.00B and IoT reached $7.13B—and core Arm/Nuvia litigation risk remains contained pending Third Circuit appeal and Delaware bench remedies—audited FY2026 Form 10-K footnotes and November 2026 filings expose material frictions: Handsets fell 13.4% (-26% in Q4) on Apple's internal C2 modem rollout; two customers represent 42% of revenue and China (incl. Hong Kong) represents 42% ($18.08B); QCT EBT margin compressed 330 bps to 27.1% alongside $8.64B inventory (156 DIO) and $18.6B in unconditional purchase obligations ($13.8B due in FY27); GAAP Net Income ($13.63B) was flattered by a $5.7B CAMT valuation allowance release ($4.21B net tax benefit vs. $1,644M cash taxes paid); ~$6.0B in FY26 M&A (Alphawave $2.27B, Modular $2.62B, plus 8 bolt-ons) swelled goodwill +44% to $16.37B and issued 46M shares against 48M repurchased ($7,817M buybacks + $3,854M dividends = 135% of $8.65B FCF), leaving ending shares nearly flat (-0.2% to 1,072M) with $3.45B SBC ($4.1B unrecognized RSU backlog) and a 25M-share ($1.8B) AWS contra-revenue warrant; and a Nov 12/13, 2026 $4.0B senior notes offering lifted pro forma debt to $17.10B ($9.66B pro forma cash). Compounding durability hinges on FY2027 Data Center ($5B target) and Auto/IoT outpacing Apple erosion and dilution.
